learning_outcomes.text_as_printed: Define matter and understand that everything around us is made of matter.
Identify and classify different materials (matter) based on their properties such as hardness, softness, solubility, and brittleness.
Explain that matter is made up of very small particles called particles.
Recognize the three states of matter — solid, liquid, and gas — and describe their characteristics.
Demonstrate that matter occupies space and has mass.
Describe how matter change states when heated or cooled (melting, boiling, condensation, freezing).
Understand the concepts of expansion and contraction of matter when heated or cooled.
Perform simple experiments to observe the properties and changes in matter.
Explain the concept of sublimation with examples like naphthalene.
Identify examples of solids, liquids, and gases from everyday life.
Describe how particles are arranged differently in solids, liquids, and gases.
Understand that air is matter and it has weight.
Explain that matter cannot occupy the same space at the same time as another matter.
Develop observational skills through activities related to properties of matter.
